Minimum of 2 years of hands-on experience performing general facility maintenance, building construction, or multi-trade repairs.
5 years of construction experience
Demonstrated experience supervising volunteers and temporary employees

Facilities and Grounds Management: Repair and maintenance of facilities and grounds, including painting, carpentry, electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling systems (air conditioners, propane heaters and stoves, refrigeration units), water systems (waterlines and trenches, well pumps, storage tanks, filters and general plumbing), backup power generators, roads and berms, gates and fences, trails and signs. Maintain, repair, and drive vehicles, tractors, trailers and other transport systems as needed. Organize and maintain tools, supplies and maintenance facilities (e.g., shops, sheds, yards). Custodial duties include: sweeping, mopping, cleaning sinks and toilets, washing windows and screens, dusting furniture, and trash and recycling removal. Inspect and maintain fire safety systems and equipment and supplies. Maintain a safe, visually aesthetic and functional landscape around facilities that incorporates native plant horticulture and schemes that preserve the environmental and cultural/historical integrity of the reserve. Work with part-time employees and supervise volunteers. (60% time)

User Management and General Administration: Responsible for reserve operations when other reserve staff are off-site or on extended absences, including operation of main office and communications. Assist the Resident Director and other staff as needed with visitor use of facilities for research, teaching and outreach activities. Assist with user arrival/departure, including preparing lodging, use of laboratory and classroom, communicating Deep Canyon rules and regulations, check-out inspections, and billing or fee collection. Support researchers and classes with equipment and utility needs. Coordinate reserve use to avoid impacts and conflicts among other users. Select and purchase supplies and equipment following UCR Purchasing policies. Perform accounting tasks as needed and maintain all files and records. Assist with management of user applications and reservations including RAMS documentation and sign-in sheets, billing invoices, and correspondence as needed. Under the direction of the Reserve Director, assist in organizing workshops, meetings, and conferences; participate in public outreach activities including teaching, guided tours, and lectures/demonstrations. (20% time)

Construction: As directed and supervised by the Resident Director, participate in the design and construction of small projects involving facilities repairs, renovations and upgrades, campground facilities, storage facilities, decking, walkways, bird feeders or other research and educational props. Assist other reserve and UCR staff with planning, design and implementation of major facilities additions and upgrades. Facilitate and work with vendors and construction contractors as needed. (15% time)

Resource Management Provide skilled labor and applied techniques in support on-going management or research projects, including erosion control, native vegetation restoration and protection, rare species habitat management and protection of archaeological sites. Perform regular patrols to maintain reserve boundaries and redirect public trespass. Assist in recording and maintaining on-site climate and other data monitoring systems. (5% time)

High level skills in facilities maintenance and construction, including carpentry, electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling systems, well systems, painting, fencing.
Ability to read and interpret building plans, and to implement new construction based on plans.
Knowledge of maintenance for a variety of vehicles and engines, including tractors, 4WD trucks, passenger vehicles, small motors (generators, power tools, etc.)
Experience operating tractors with backhoe and front end loader

Demonstrated experience using hand tools, power tools (including table saws, drills and compressors), and equipment (including tractors, hitch trailers, concrete mixers) appropriate for general maintenance and construction of buildings and grounds.

Demonstrated hands-on skill in advanced construction trades - including framing, roofing, drywall, propane/water lines, welding, and masonry - as well as basic vehicle, motor, and equipment maintenance and repair.
Basic understanding of barbed wire and chain link fence construction and maintenance.
Working knowledge and practical understanding of California building codes and environmental safety policies applicable to remote or specialized facilities.
Working knowledge of facility maintenance practices and procedures across multiple trades (including carpentry, plumbing, and electrical), as well as general safety policies and procedures.

Basic understanding of state and federal agencies and regulatory policies that apply to research and land management issues, and general knowledge of conservation issues in relation to reserve management.
Written communication skills to prepare a variety of correspondence, reports, policies and procedures, and training documents.
Active listening, interpersonal communication and problem-solving skills to effectively resolve questions, concerns, issues or problems and ensure cooperative and productive working relationships.
Skills to work independently and as part of a team.
Working organizational skills to work on multiple projects with competing deadlines, to establish goals and workload priorities, and to meet project deadlines within budget and time constraints.
Working knowledge of workplace safety guidelines, emergency preparedness, and hazardous materials handling.
